newsitem.title: GERMANY: Opel says hard to match 1996 profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Opel says hard to match 1996 profit in 1997.

text.p: German carmaker Adam Opel AG, the German unit of General Motors Corp, said on Thursday it would not be easy to achieve the 1996 net profit level of 314 million marks ($181.4 million) in 1997.

Opel managing director David Herman said in the text of a speech at the carmaker's annual news conference he did not see strong economic growth signals nor any change in the conditions of the European vehicle industry.

Hennig Klages, the Opel management board member in charge of finance, said another factor influencing profit would be the phase-out of the current Astra model during the year ahead of the launch of a new model in 1998.
Opel earlier on Thursday said its 1996 net profit was 314 million marks compared with 363 million marks in 1995.
